expectation: Membrane ring on macrophages (M2-like), some dendritic cells and endothelium. In gut-like tissue, expect common scattered single cells in the lamina propria and submucosa, sitting under the epithelium and near vessels, mostly on a subset of CD163+ cells.
observed: A: dense yellow speckle of single cells in the stromal and submucosal bands, with fainter haze over the epithelium. B/C: bright puncta lining the basal edge of the epithelium. D: a bright cell with a ring-like outline. E: many CD206 cells sit on CD163 cells (white), and some CD206+ cells are CD163-negative.
why: Discrete CD206+ cells are concentrated in the stroma under the epithelium, and many of them overlap CD163 cells in E, as expected for macrophages.
notes: Scattered punctate cells fill the stromal bands and line the base of the epithelium. In row E they largely fall on CD163 cells. There is mild epithelial haze and some bright debris, but the cell population is clear.
